issues.legal_issue: A claim to cut and appropriate forest produce under an unregistered grant does not establish an infringement of fundamental rights when the grant, under any available construction, gives no enforceable property right against the State.
material_facts: The claimant relied on an unregistered instrument granting rights to take wood and other forest produce from land for a period of years.
Proprietary rights in the land vested in the State under a later enactment.
The claimant alleged that the State forest officer’s order stopping the cutting infringed her rights under Articles 19(1)(f) and 19(1)(g).
issues.conclusion: The order did not infringe the claimed fundamental rights, and the Article 32 petition was dismissed. Depending on the instrument’s construction, a proprietary interest was ineffective for want of registration and, in any event, vested in the State; a licence ended when the grantor’s proprietary rights vested; a profit à prendre was an unregistered interest in immovable property; or a purely personal contractual right remained with the claimant and could be pursued through an ordinary suit, not as a fundamental-rights claim against the State.
issues.legal_principle: A petition under Article 32 requires an infringement of a fundamental right. Under the Registration Act, an unregistered instrument does not affect immovable property or transfer an interest in it. Section 3 of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950 vested proprietary rights in the State. A profit à prendre is an interest in immovable property and requires registration. A purely personal contractual right does not become a fundamental right merely because its performance is obstructed; its enforcement or breach is ordinarily pursued by suit. The Court followed Ananda Behera v. State of Orissa and did not follow Chhotabai Jethabai Patel and Co. v. State of Madhya Pradesh.

rule.if: article_32_fundamental_rights_petition and rights_claimed_under_unregistered_forest_grant and ((grant_conveys_proprietary_interest and proprietary_interest_vested_in_state) or (grant_creates_profit_a_prendre and profit_is_immovable_property) or (grant_is_pure_license and grantor_proprietary_rights_vested_in_state) or (grant_is_personal_contract and state_not_party_to_contract and state_did_not_acquire_contract))

predicates.article_32_fundamental_rights_petition: The claimant brought a constitutional petition seeking relief for an alleged infringement of fundamental rights.
predicates.rights_claimed_under_unregistered_forest: The claimant based the asserted rights to enter forest land and take its produce on an instrument that was not registered.
predicates.grant_conveys_proprietary_interest: The instrument, as construed, purports to transfer a proprietary interest in land.
predicates.proprietary_interest_vested_in_state: The proprietary interest in the land vested in the State under a later enactment.
predicates.grant_creates_profit_a_prendre: The instrument, as construed, grants a right to enter land and take produce from it.
predicates.profit_is_immovable_property: The granted right is an interest in land treated as immovable property.
predicates.grant_is_pure_license: The instrument, as construed, grants only permission to enter the land.
predicates.grantor_proprietary_rights_vested_in_sta: The grantor’s proprietary rights in the land vested in the State.
predicates.grant_is_personal_contract: The instrument, as construed, gives the claimant only a personal contractual right.
predicates.state_not_party_to_contract: The State was not a party to the contract.
predicates.state_did_not_acquire_contract: The State did not acquire or take possession of the claimant’s contractual right.

issues.definition: When a fundamental-rights petition rests on an unregistered forest grant, and the grant falls within any of the stated categories, the grant does not establish a fundamental-rights infringement by the State.

issues.legal_issue: A grant allowing trees to remain and grow before felling, rather than covering only timber ready for prompt removal, concerns immovable property and must be registered to pass an interest in it.
material_facts: The instrument granted forest-cutting rights for a term of years and covered trees that were not yet fit to be felled.
The claimant could leave trees standing and fell them later, including when they reached the required size during the term.
The instrument was unregistered, and the asserted fundamental right depended on rights under that instrument.
issues.conclusion: In the separate opinion, the grant was held to include immovable property as well as standing timber; because the instrument was compulsorily registrable and unregistered, it passed no title or interest on which an enforceable fundamental right could rest.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(26) of the General Clauses Act and section 2(6) of the Registration Act, trees attached to the earth are immovable property, subject to the distinction for standing timber. Section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act excludes standing timber from immovable property, but trees that may continue growing and drawing nourishment from the soil are not merely standing timber. An instrument transferring an interest in such trees requires registration; if unregistered, it passes no title or interest. The separate opinion relied on Ananda Behera v. State of Orissa and treated it as controlling over the inconsistent approach in Chhotabai Jethabai Patel and Co. v. State of Madhya Pradesh.

rule.if: article_32_fundamental_rights_petition and rights_claimed_under_unregistered_forest_grant and grant_covers_trees_not_ready_for_immediate_felling and grant_allows_trees_to_remain_and_grow and grant_is_not_limited_to_timber_for_prompt_removal

predicates.article_32_fundamental_rights_petition: The claimant sought constitutional relief for an alleged infringement of fundamental rights.
predicates.rights_claimed_under_unregistered_forest: The claimant based the asserted forest-cutting rights on an instrument that was not registered.
predicates.grant_covers_trees_not_ready_for_immedia: The instrument covers trees that are not fit to be felled when the grant is made.
predicates.grant_allows_trees_to_remain_and_grow: The claimant may leave covered trees standing so they continue to grow before felling them.
predicates.grant_is_not_limited_to_timber_for_promp: The grant extends beyond timber intended for prompt removal and use.

issues.definition: When an unregistered forest grant covers trees that may continue growing before they are felled, the grant passes no enforceable interest.
